---
title: "How to extract raw snippets to send to the IBL"
---

This guide is for labs that share Neuropixels recordings with the IBL. The recordings are too
large to move, so you run one command per probe. It reads your SpikeGLX recording, keeps five
short snippets of the raw AP and LF data, adds the probe geometry, and writes the result
to an `.h5` file that you send to us. Several probes can go into the same file. Nothing is
filtered or otherwise processed, so we can try different analyses without asking you for
more data.

## Prerequisites

- Python 3.12 or newer
- A SpikeGLX recording of the probe: the `.ap.bin` or `.ap.cbin` file with its `.meta` file
  next to it. The `.lf.bin` / `.lf.cbin` file is used when it is next to the AP file.
- Supported probes: Neuropixels 1.0, 3A and 2.x (including four-shank 2.4). Neuropixels 2
  records no separate LF band, so only the wideband data is stored. If your probe type is
  not supported, the command stops and says so; please tell us the probe type.

## Install

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/int-brain-lab/ibleatools@<tag>
```

Use the tag we gave you in place of `<tag>`. This installs ibleatools and its dependencies,
which is a large install.

## Extract the snippets

Run the command once per probe:

```bash
ibleatools-snippets /data/probe00/run_g0_t0.imec0.ap.cbin \
    -o /data/to_send/VF066_2025-12-04.h5
```

- `-o` is the file to write. If it does not exist it is created; if it exists, the probe is
  added to it (see "Several probes in one file"). Name it so that you can tell the subject and
  date apart.
- `--name` is optional. It is the name of the probe's recording inside the file; the default is
  the AP file name without `.ap.bin` / `.ap.cbin`.

By default the command takes 5 snippets of 5 s, spread over the recording and leaving out the
first and last 5 minutes. Options for other cases:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--t-starts 600 900` | Snippet start times in seconds, instead of automatic ones |
| `--n-snippets`, `--duration` | Number and length (s) of the automatic snippets |
| `--margin` | Seconds skipped at each end; lower it for recordings shorter than about 10 minutes |

`ibleatools-snippets --help` lists everything.

## Several probes in one file

Run the command for each probe with the same `-o`. The first run creates the file and each
later run adds a recording to it:

```bash
ibleatools-snippets probe00/run_g0_t0.imec0.ap.cbin -o VF066_2025-12-04.h5
ibleatools-snippets probe01/run_g0_t0.imec1.ap.cbin -o VF066_2025-12-04.h5
```

- Each probe is stored as a recording named after its AP file, here `run_g0_t0.imec0` and
  `run_g0_t0.imec1`. When two recordings would get the same name, for example probes that are
  both called `imec0` in different folders, pass `--name` for at least one of them. If the name
  is taken, the command stops and says so; it never overwrites a recording.
- When a probe is added to an existing file, do not interrupt the command between the log line
  that ends "smaller than the raw data" and the line that starts "Added recording". The probe
  is copied into your file in that short step, and an interruption there can damage the file.
  Interrupting at any other time leaves the existing file as it was.
- Do not run two commands on the same file at the same time.

If a run fails, the command prints the reason and exits with a non-zero code, so a script
that loops over probes can check the exit code.

## What the file holds

- The raw AP and LF samples of each snippet, compressed without loss, with the gains to
  convert them to volts.
- The probe geometry, each channel's shank, the original `.meta` text, and the start time of
  each snippet in your recording.

The SpikeGLX sync channel is not included. A Neuropixels 1.0 probe adds about 0.23 GB to the
file with the defaults (5 snippets of 5 s).

## Send us the files

Send us the `.h5` files. One file can hold all probes of a session, as described above, so
repeat the command with the same `-o` for each probe.
